task.title: The board conflict banner is cleared by the next one-second poll, so a conflict report is never read
task.description:
Deferred from the adversarial review of PR #29 (WB-01KZBT3J1AMW4E5F688WPNZGJZ). PR #29 moved reportIntentFailure to after the forced refresh in drainIntents' catch (internal/webui/assets/index.html), which stops the *forced* refresh from erasing the report before it is drawn. It does not make the report readable: window.setInterval(refresh, 1000) fires a poll every second and every successful refresh sets stale.dataset.visible = 'false'. So after a board conflict the banner is guaranteed to be wiped in under a second, and a user who is not looking at that corner of the screen never sees it - in exactly the shared-beta multi-writer scenario the parent ticket exists for.

The client tests cannot catch this by construction: clientDOMHarness captures setInterval into intervalCallback and never invokes it, and TestHandlerClientStaleWriteRollsBackRefreshesAndRebasesTheQueue asserts stale.dataset.visible === 'true' synchronously right after the drain settles.

Deliberately not patched with a timer or a sticky flag in PR #29. The design doc already argues that per-card reporting is the right home for an intent failure - the card has no message affordance today, pendingTaskMessages serves the detail view rather than the board, and inventing one is a UI design question. The short-lived banner is the same missing affordance, so it belongs with that work rather than with a suppression rule bolted onto refresh(). The in-code comment and the design doc were both corrected in PR #29 to state that the report survives at most one poll tick.

What good looks like: an intent failure is reported on or beside the card it concerns, and the report persists until the user has had a chance to act on it rather than until the next poll.
